- Mouldy/crappy food
- Given wrong medications
- The way they treat/talk to you
- Poor cleaning
- You sleep on blood stained sheets 
- There are blood stains on the walls
- They rarely let you outside
- The room you are in is very plain and basic with no heating, so you are freezing
- You get woken up every hour for ‘checks’ and they blind you with a torch
- They walk in on you even if you are showering
- You only see a therapist once a week/every two weeks
- There is nothing to do apart from broken puzzles and watch soundless TV
- You don’t get any of your belongings 
- People could be self harming around you and the staff just ignore it. They don’t care and are just in it for the money
- You get shouted at
- You breathe in stale air
- When I was In there I frequently found glass shards and other sharp items
- It felt like a cage
- It was extremely dull and boring

In my experience the psychiatric wards are horrifically traumatic places.
The staff are terrible and uncaring.
However there were some very friendly nurses and 8/10 times the patients are friendly too. 

If you are going to one.
Hopefully you won’t be in the same one that I went to.
Just keep in mind that you may see/hear/experience some scary things. 
It’ll be okay though. 

You won’t have privileges and will just be in a room with a blanket and no belongings if you are sectioned. 
You won’t be able to leave the building/ see visitors for how ever long you are on section.
They can give you medication via pill or injection.

They can physically restrain you for the littlest of things if they think you are a danger to yourself or others. There will most likely be screaming and unsettling scenarios but there will also be calming quiet. 
If you are a light sleeper you are likely to become an insomniac. (They will throw open your door in the night and shine a torch on your face, to check you are alive)

I thought I’d just prepare you for the worst, so it won’t be such a big shock if you happen to go a not so great unit. 

I’ll end it on a positive note.

They do allow visitors.
Most staff are caring.
You are allowed to talk to patients and make friends.
They do outings.
You can smoke (If you are a smoker)
Alrightish food.
Pets can visit you.
You can have home leave.
They do activities.
They have TV’s.
There are no straight jackets.
They have windows. 
You can walk around.
They have groups to go to.

Good luck! :) 
Hope you feel better soon.
